scispace.question: How does the HyRec effective multilevel atom method eliminate excited hydrogen states in a quasi-steady approximation during cosmological recombination, and what is assumed about time derivatives and atomic population storage?
scispace.date_caveat: Some repository duplicate records carry 2022 ingestion dates; use original publication dates below.

exa.html_date_caveat: 1006.1355 HTML contains a later conversion date; it does not replace the original publication date.

primary_papers.title: Ultrafast effective multilevel atom method for primordial hydrogen recombination
primary_papers.used_sections: Section III, especially equations 12–14 and the steady-state construction
primary_papers.supported_point: Excited-state equations are evaluated in the steady-state approximation; effective atomic coefficients and cosmological evolution are separated. This does not assert finite excited-state storage is exactly evolved.

primary_papers.title: HyRec: A fast and highly accurate primordial hydrogen and helium recombination code
primary_papers.used_sections: Effective interface-state and radiative-transfer construction, especially Section III
primary_papers.supported_point: The method combines effective atomic states with a radiation solve; virtual radiation bins must not be treated as additional physical atomic inventory levels.

novelty_scope: Direct inverse-transfer and finite-storage identities are derived in the accompanying note; no new general theorem or unperformed numerical physical validation is claimed.
